source.title: YellowFin and the Art of Momentum Tuning
source.authors: Jian Zhang; Ioannis Mitliagkas; C. Ré

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out validation performance of adaptive and momentum SGD optimizers, but does not test the original random-label setup or the full scope of the claim.
record.gate_note: Only held-out comparisons in Section 5.1 are included. Training-loss speedups and cited prior-work findings are not held-out generalization results for V4.
record.test_reason: The study independently compares momentum SGD with Adam on held-out language-modeling and parsing metrics under limited learning-rate tuning. Configurations are selected by training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but matching hand-tuned momentum SGD refers specifically to training loss. The authors conclude that YellowFin automatically tunes learning rate and momentum, matches tuned momentum SGD's training loss, and improves validation metrics over tuned Adam on the plotted LSTM tasks. They also report synchronous and asynchronous convergence speedups.
record.recipe_differences: Uses tuned momentum SGD, tuned Adam, and an automatic momentum SGD tuner; does not use the original random-label memorization protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer choice; PTB is an exception for momentum SGD's reported validation advantage.

fits_no_version.finding: On German-English translation, YellowFin with adaptive clipping reaches validation BLEU4 31.59 versus 30.75 for manually clipped Nesterov momentum SGD after 120 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatic momentum tuning and adaptive clipping can improve translation performance relative to a fixed momentum-SGD recipe.

record.peer_reviewed: USENIX workshop on Tackling computer systems problems with machine learning techniques
record.problems: Held-out comparisons are plotted without numerical validation values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments compare optimizer recipes and do not measure the generalization gap directly.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.

Independent image-classification held-out comparisons; broader optimizer hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; optimizer switching. The eligible comparisons do not demonstrate worse Adam validation performance despite equal or better training performance. PTB's validation ordering cannot be established from the supplied text.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and their correlation with generalization gaps. Optimization curvature estimates do not test this.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is assigned to R1: being an exception to SGD's advantage does not establish a tie or Adam advantage. Proposed-method comparisons, including Appendix J.4, are excluded under the supplied row rule. Appendix J.4 reports YellowFin tuning improvements from 88.7 to 80.5 perplexity and 92.63% to 94.75% accuracy, plus advantages over searched Adam; these are method-evaluation results. Contrary to the record's blanket uncertainty statement, experiments average three seeds and the introduction reports normalized test-metric standard deviations of 0.05%–0.6%, without comparator-specific uncertainty for these rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Only comparisons on this paper's models and recipes; broader benchmarks, wider tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

relationships.condition: TinyShakespeare character-level LSTM and WSJ constituency-parsing LSTM; learning-rate grids with SGD momentum fixed at 0.9.
relationships.reason: Section 5.1 explicitly reports better validation perplexity and F1 for momentum SGD than Adam in R2 and R3; momentum SGD also achieves better training loss.
